checklist.title: Falsify Post-Condition: Can upgrade_to_fulu produce a post-state where fork.current_version != FULU_FORK_VERSION?

reachability.notes: Wrong fork version causes complete P2P network isolation.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify the upgrade_to_fulu function in each CL client implementation (e.g., consensus-specs/specs/fulu/fork.py or equivalent). 2. Verify the Fork object is constructed with current=FULU_FORK_VERSION as a hardcoded constant. 3. Check that no conditional logic could cause FULU_FORK_VERSION to be substituted or omitted. 4. Write a test that calls upgrade_to_fulu with a valid Electra pre-state and asserts post.fork.current_version == FULU_FORK_VERSION. 5. Attempt to falsify by modifying the pre-state's fork.current_version to various invalid values and verifying the post-state still has FULU_FORK_VERSION. 6. Cross-check that FULU_FORK_VERSION constant is consistent across all CL client configurations.
executable_checks: Unit test: assert upgrade_to_fulu(electra_state).fork.current_version == FULU_FORK_VERSION
Differential test: run upgrade_to_fulu across multiple CL implementations and compare post.fork.current_version
Property-based test: forall valid electra states, post.fork.current_version == FULU_FORK_VERSION
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0006, Invariant: fork-SG-002-INV-003, Assumption: asm-009. Incorrect fork version would cause complete P2P network isolation since fork digest (used for gossip topic subscription) depends on current_version. This is a CRITICAL internal correctness property.

checklist.title: Falsify Post-Condition: Can upgrade_to_fulu produce a post-state where fork.epoch != get_current_epoch(pre)?

reachability.notes: Incorrect fork epoch in state would affect epoch-dependent logic.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify the Fork construction in upgrade_to_fulu where epoch is assigned. 2. Verify that the epoch value is derived from get_current_epoch(pre) and not from any other source (e.g., FULU_FORK_EPOCH constant, hardcoded value, or state.slot directly). 3. Write a test: given pre-state at slot S, verify post.fork.epoch == compute_epoch_at_slot(S). 4. Test edge case: pre-state at the exact first slot of FULU_FORK_EPOCH. 5. Attempt to falsify: check if any client implementation uses FULU_FORK_EPOCH directly instead of get_current_epoch(pre), which would be correct in normal operation but could diverge in testing or unusual configurations.
executable_checks: Unit test: assert upgrade_to_fulu(pre).fork.epoch == get_current_epoch(pre)
Edge case test: verify fork.epoch at the exact FULU_FORK_EPOCH boundary
Differential test: compare fork.epoch across CL implementations for same pre-state
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0007, Invariant: fork-SG-002-INV-004, Assumption: asm-009. Incorrect fork epoch could affect all downstream epoch-dependent computations including committee assignments, proposer selection, and sync committee rotations.

checklist.title: Falsify Post-Condition: Can upgrade_to_fulu produce a post-state where proposer_lookahead != initialize_proposer_lookahead(pre)?
checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify the proposer_lookahead assignment in upgrade_to_fulu. 2. Verify it calls initialize_proposer_lookahead(pre) and not some other initialization (e.g., empty list, zeros, or initialize_proposer_lookahead(post)). 3. Critically check: is the argument 'pre' (the Electra state) or 'post' (the partially constructed Fulu state)? Using post could cause incorrect initialization since post may have different fork data. 4. Write a test comparing upgrade_to_fulu(pre).proposer_lookahead against independently computed initialize_proposer_lookahead(pre). 5. Test with various validator set sizes and compositions. 6. Check that initialize_proposer_lookahead is deterministic for the same input.
executable_checks: Unit test: assert upgrade_to_fulu(pre).proposer_lookahead == initialize_proposer_lookahead(pre)
Differential test: compare proposer_lookahead across CL implementations after fork
Property-based test: forall pre-states, proposer_lookahead is consistent with pre-state validator set
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0008, Invariant: fork-SG-002-INV-005, Assumption: asm-017. This is the EIP-7917 (Deterministic Proposer Lookahead) initialization at fork time. Incorrect initialization would cause wrong proposer assignments post-fork, potentially allowing unauthorized block proposals or causing consensus divergence.

checklist.title: Falsify Invariant: Can upgrade_to_fulu mutate the pre-state object?

reachability.notes: Pre-state mutation would cause non-deterministic behavior but is hard to exploit externally. Requires further investigation: scope depends on whether pre-state mutation can be triggered to cause observable consensus divergence.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Serialize the pre-state (deep copy or hash) before calling upgrade_to_fulu. 2. Call upgrade_to_fulu(pre). 3. Serialize the pre-state again and compare with the original. 4. Focus on implementation languages where references are shared by default (Python, Java, Go). In Python (reference spec), check if any field is modified in-place rather than copied. 5. Specifically verify that mutable container fields (validators list, balances list, pending operations lists) are not shared between pre and post states. 6. Attempt to falsify: after calling upgrade_to_fulu, modify a field in the returned post-state and verify the pre-state is unaffected.

code_locations.line_range: Entire function body - all field copy operations

executable_checks: Unit test: hash(pre_before) == hash(pre_after) where upgrade_to_fulu is called between
Mutation test: modify post-state after upgrade and verify pre-state is unchanged
Memory reference test (language-specific): verify no shared mutable references between pre and post
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0009, Invariant: fork-SG-002-INV-006. CONDITIONAL SCOPE: Pre-state mutation is an internal implementation concern but could cause non-deterministic state transitions if the pre-state is reused after the fork (e.g., for fork choice or reorg handling). Requires further investigation to determine exploitability.

checklist.title: Falsify Invariant: Can compute_fork_version return ambiguous results or take multiple branches for any epoch value?

reachability.notes: Used in fork digest computation for P2P topic subscription.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Examine the compute_fork_version function's conditional logic (if/elif/else chain). 2. Verify that conditions are mutually exclusive and exhaustive. Specifically check that the ordering of conditions matches the epoch ordering: FULU >= epoch checks come before ELECTRA >= epoch checks, etc. 3. Test at every fork epoch boundary: epoch = FULU_FORK_EPOCH, FULU_FORK_EPOCH-1, ELECTRA_FORK_EPOCH, etc. 4. Test epoch = 0 (genesis) and epoch = MAX_UINT64 (overflow edge case). 5. Verify no off-by-one errors at boundaries (>= vs >). 6. Cross-compare outputs across all CL implementations for the same epoch values.

code_locations.line_range: Conditional chain for fork version selection

executable_checks: Exhaustive test: for every fork epoch boundary +/- 1, verify exactly one branch is taken
Property-based test: forall epoch >= 0, compute_fork_version returns a valid 4-byte version
Differential test: compare compute_fork_version output across CL clients for boundary epochs
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0011, Invariant: p2p-SG-001-INV-002. This function is critical for P2P topic subscription. An ambiguous fork version would cause nodes to subscribe to wrong gossip topics, fragmenting the network.

checklist.title: Falsify Invariant: Can compute_fork_version return null, error, or invalid value for any epoch >= 0?

reachability.notes: A null fork version would crash P2P message handling.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Review compute_fork_version for any code path that could raise an exception, return None/null, or panic. 2. Check if the else/default case is present and returns GENESIS_FORK_VERSION. 3. In statically typed languages (Go, Rust, Java), verify the function always returns a valid Version type. 4. Test with epoch = 0, epoch = 1, epoch = MAX_UINT64, and epoch values between all fork boundaries. 5. In implementations that use match/switch statements, verify there is a default arm. 6. For implementations with configuration-driven fork epochs, test with FAR_FUTURE_EPOCH configurations where some forks are disabled.

code_locations.line_range: Entire function including all branches and default case

executable_checks: Edge case test: compute_fork_version(0) returns GENESIS_FORK_VERSION
Edge case test: compute_fork_version(MAX_UINT64) returns FULU_FORK_VERSION
Fuzz test: random epoch values never cause exception or null return
Configuration test: with FAR_FUTURE_EPOCH forks, function still returns valid version
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0012, Invariant: p2p-SG-001-INV-003. A null or error return during P2P handshake or gossip validation would crash the node. This is especially dangerous at fork boundaries where the function is called frequently.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is data column sidecar index properly bounds-checked before processing?

reachability.notes: An attacker can craft a sidecar with an out-of-range index and send it via P2P gossip.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify verify_data_column_sidecar in each CL client implementation. 2. Verify that sidecar.index >= NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS check exists and occurs BEFORE any array indexing operations that use sidecar.index. 3. Check for integer overflow: if NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS is 128 and sidecar.index is a uint64, can a crafted value bypass the check? 4. Send a sidecar with index = NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS (off-by-one boundary) and verify rejection. 5. Send a sidecar with index = MAX_UINT64 and verify rejection without crash. 6. Verify the rejection returns the correct gossip validation result (REJECT, not IGNORE) to prevent repeated attempts. 7. Check that the column index is validated in both gossip and RPC (req/resp) paths.

code_locations.function: Data column processing functions that use sidecar.index as array index

executable_checks: P2P test: send sidecar with index = NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS and verify REJECT response
P2P test: send sidecar with index = MAX_UINT64 and verify no crash
Off-by-one test: send sidecar with index = NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS - 1 (valid) and verify acceptance
Fuzz test: random column indices, verify no out-of-bounds access
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0013, Invariant: p2p-SG-002-INV-001, Trust Boundary: tb-001. This is a CRITICAL boundary check on the P2P gossip validation path. PeerDAS (EIP-7594) introduces data column sidecars as a new P2P message type. An attacker-controlled index could cause array out-of-bounds crashes in any CL client.

checklist.title: Verify Internal Node Safety: Does beacon node safely handle column index in all downstream operations?

reachability.notes: Even with boundary validation, check that all downstream uses of sidecar.index are safe.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Trace all usages of sidecar.index after it passes the boundary check. 2. Verify that column array accesses in custody computation, KZG proof verification, and data reconstruction all use the validated index. 3. Check if any intermediate computation could re-derive or modify the index in an unsafe way. 4. Verify that the gossip topic subscription index (data_column_sidecar_{subnet_id}) is consistent with the sidecar.index validation.
executable_checks: Code review: trace all uses of sidecar.index after validation
Integration test: process valid sidecar through full pipeline and verify no panics
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0013 (supporting node check). Ensures that even after boundary validation, the index is used safely throughout the data column processing pipeline.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is empty kzg_commitments properly rejected in data column sidecar validation?

reachability.notes: Attacker can craft sidecar with empty commitments and send via gossip.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify the kzg_commitments length check in verify_data_column_sidecar. 2. Verify the check occurs: len(sidecar.kzg_commitments) == 0 causes rejection. 3. Check what happens if the check is missing: trace all downstream uses of kzg_commitments that could divide by len(kzg_commitments) or iterate assuming non-empty. 4. Send a sidecar with empty kzg_commitments via gossip and verify rejection. 5. Check if KZG proof verification functions handle empty inputs gracefully or crash. 6. Verify that the column cell count computation (which depends on kzg_commitments length) handles zero correctly.

code_locations.line_range: Functions that iterate over or index into kzg_commitments

executable_checks: P2P test: send sidecar with empty kzg_commitments and verify REJECT
Crash test: verify no division-by-zero or index-out-of-bounds with empty commitments
Integration test: verify KZG proof verification handles empty input without panic
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0014, Invariant: p2p-SG-002-INV-002, Trust Boundary: tb-001. Empty kzg_commitments in a data column sidecar is an invalid state. Blocks with blob transactions always have at least one commitment. An empty commitments list could trigger division-by-zero in cell count calculations or cause KZG verification to behave unexpectedly.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is kzg_commitments count properly bounded by epoch-dependent max_blobs_per_block?

reachability.notes: Attacker can craft sidecar with excessive commitments. The epoch-dependent limit adds complexity.

checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify the kzg_commitments upper bound check in verify_data_column_sidecar. 2. Verify it uses get_blob_parameters(compute_epoch_at_slot(sidecar.slot)).max_blobs_per_block as the limit. 3. CRITICAL: Check that the epoch is derived from the sidecar's slot, not the current node's slot. An attacker could send a sidecar for a future/past epoch with different blob parameters. 4. Test at epoch boundaries where max_blobs_per_block changes (BPO hardfork boundaries per EIP-7892). Send a sidecar for the new epoch with the old limit's number of commitments. 5. Send a sidecar with len(kzg_commitments) = max_blobs_per_block + 1 and verify rejection. 6. Send a sidecar with len(kzg_commitments) = max_blobs_per_block (boundary) and verify acceptance. 7. Verify consistent behavior across CL clients at BPO parameter change epochs.
executable_checks: P2P test: send sidecar with commitments count = max_blobs_per_block + 1 and verify REJECT
Boundary test: send sidecar at BPO epoch boundary where max_blobs_per_block changes
Off-by-one test: send sidecar with commitments count = max_blobs_per_block (valid boundary)
Differential test: compare max_blobs_per_block resolution across CL clients at same epoch
Memory test: send sidecar with extremely large commitments count and verify no excessive allocation before rejection
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0015, Invariant: p2p-SG-002-INV-003, Trust Boundary: tb-001, Assumption: asm-015. EIP-7892 (Blob Parameter Only Hardforks) makes max_blobs_per_block epoch-dependent, adding complexity to this validation. The most interesting attack surface is at BPO epoch boundaries where the limit changes. If different CL clients use different epoch values for the lookup, consensus divergence could result.
